references.text: Parallel account in Matthew where Jesus threatens the demon and it leaves the boy, and he was healed from that hour.
Parallel account in Mark where Jesus threatens the unclean spirit, commands it to come out, and the boy is healed.
Jesus threatens an unclean spirit and commands it to come out, an early example of Jesus' authority over unclean spirits.
Jesus threatens an unclean spirit and commands it to leave a man, and the demon throws him down but comes out without harming him – the same pattern of threat and healing.
Jesus gives a son back to his mother, parallel to how Jesus here gives the boy back to his father – the motif of returning a child to the parent.
Elijah returns the raised boy to his mother, a motif that Luke seems to echo when Jesus returns the boy to his father.
Jesus commands the unclean spirit to leave a man – showing Jesus' authority over demons by threatening them.
Jesus had given the disciples power over all evil spirits and to heal diseases, which forms the background for their inability to drive out the demon in this account.
Peter summarizes Jesus' ministry: he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil – a summary that includes events like this one.
